title: "RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)"
description: "A system design pattern that retrieves external information and supplies it to a generative model when answering a request."
term: "RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)"
letter: "R"
category: "LLM Engineering"
difficulty: "Intermediate"

## Simple explanation

Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) lets a language model consult a
collection of relevant information while answering. Instead of relying only
on what was learned during training, the application searches for useful
passages and includes them with the question.

## Technical explanation

A RAG pipeline typically indexes documents, retrieves candidate passages
for a query, and supplies selected context to a generative model. Retrieval
may use lexical search, dense embeddings, or a hybrid approach; optional
reranking can improve the selected context. Generation remains dependent on
the evidence, prompt, and model behavior.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

RAG can connect a model to private, changing, or domain-specific sources
without retraining the base model. It also introduces data ingestion,
retrieval quality, access control, freshness, citation, and evaluation
requirements that must be designed as part of the system.

## How it works

Documents are prepared and indexed, often as passages with metadata. At
request time, the system retrieves and filters candidate passages, places
the relevant content in the model's context, and generates a response. The
system may return citations and should handle missing or conflicting
evidence explicitly.

The diagram omits indexing and access-control details, which are essential

## Practical example

A support assistant can retrieve passages from the current product
documentation before answering a setup question. The application can show
the passage sources so users can verify claims and notice when retrieval
misses the needed information.

## Common misconceptions

- RAG does not guarantee factual answers; retrieval can miss, and a model
  can misinterpret or ignore retrieved evidence.
- RAG is not a single algorithm. It combines retrieval, context
  construction, generation, and often additional system components.
